bib.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment

question: How much of an LLM's ability to follow instructions comes from pretraining versus large-scale instruction tuning and RLHF?
hypothesis: Superficial Alignment Hypothesis: knowledge and capabilities are learnt almost entirely during pretraining, and alignment only teaches which subdistribution of formats to use, so a small curated set should suffice.
contributions: LIMA, a 65B LLaMa fine-tuned with supervised loss on 1,000 curated prompt-response pairs, no RL or preference modelling
Human and GPT-4 preference comparison against five baselines on 300 test prompts
Ablations on data diversity, quality and quantity with 7B models
Multi-turn dialogue improved by adding 30 hand-crafted dialogue chains

method.summary: Fine-tune LLaMa 65B for 15 epochs on 1,000 hand-curated examples (750 from Stack Exchange, wikiHow, Reddit; 250 written by the authors), pick a checkpoint between epochs 5 and 10 on a 50-prompt dev set, and compare single sampled responses to five baselines with crowd workers and GPT-4. Ablations fine-tune 7B LLaMa and score with ChatGPT.
method.task: supervised instruction tuning / alignment with minimal data

datasets.name: LIMA training set
datasets.split: Stack Exchange STEM 200, Stack Exchange other 200, wikiHow 200, r/WritingPrompts 150, Natural Instructions 50, authors Group A 200
datasets.source: Stack Exchange, wikiHow, Pushshift Reddit, Super-Natural Instructions, authors
datasets.preprocessing: Stack Exchange: tau=3 sampling over 75 STEM / 99 other exchanges (5 niche discarded), title-only top-scored questions, top answer with score >= 10, drop answers under 1200 or over 4096 characters, first person, references to other answers; strip links, images, HTML except code and lists. wikiHow: 19 categories, title as prompt, body as response, 'This article...' replaced by 'The following answer...'. 13 safety prompts with refusals.

datasets.name: Dialogue chains
datasets.size: 30 chains (10 author-written, 20 edited Stack Exchange comment chains)

datasets.name: Ablation sets
datasets.size: 2,000 examples each for Stack Exchange filtered, unfiltered, wikiHow; 2K to 32K for quantity

other.eot_token: special end-of-turn token at end of each utterance

training.epochs: 15, checkpoint chosen manually between epoch 5 and 10
training.dropout: residual dropout rising linearly from 0.0 at the bottom layer to 0.3 at the last layer (0.2 for smaller models)
training.regularisation: residual dropout following Ouyang et al. 2022

other.checkpoint_selection: perplexity does not correlate with generation quality; checkpoints picked by hand on the 50-example dev set
other.ablation_note: 7B tuning with 1,000 examples possible but at least 2,000 improved stability
other.figure9: read from Fig 9: validation perplexity rises with training steps while generation quality rises

inference.samples: 1 response per test prompt per model for human study; 5 responses per test prompt in ablations

metrics.name: Pairwise preference
metrics.definition: annotator labels which of two responses is better or neither significantly better; reported as wins/ties/losses

metrics.name: Absolute Fail/Pass/Excellent
metrics.definition: manual label of 50 random LIMA responses

metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement
metrics.definition: tie-discounted accuracy: 1 point if agree, 0.5 if exactly one labelled tie, else 0; over 50 shared examples

metrics.name: ChatGPT helpfulness score
metrics.definition: 1-6 Likert from GPT-3.5 Turbo, mean over 5 samples per prompt with p=0.95 two-sided confidence interval

eval.protocol: Crowd workers and GPT-4 given identical instructions, single response per model per prompt; ablations on 7B scored by ChatGPT.

prompts.text: [Criterion]: helpfulness: "1": "Not helpful - ..." ... "6": "Highly helpful - ..." ... Does the submission meet the criterion? First, write out in a step by step manner your reasoning about the criterion to be sure that your conclusion is correct. Avoid simply stating the correct answers at the outset. Then print the choice only from "1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6" (without quotes or punctuation) on its own line corresponding to the correct answer. At the end, repeat just the selected choice again by itself on a new line.
prompts.where: Appendix D, Figure 12 (full rubric text there)

results.claim: LIMA responses are equal or preferred to GPT-4 in 43% of human comparisons.
results.setup: LIMA 65B, 1,000 examples, 300 test prompts, crowd annotators, single sampled response each
results.quote: responses from LIMA are either equivalent or strictly preferred to GPT-4 in 43% of cases

results.claim: LIMA is equal or preferred to Bard in 58% and to DaVinci003 (RLHF) in 65% of cases.
results.setup: As above; 58% vs Bard, 65% vs DaVinci003
results.quote: this statistic is as high as 58% when compared to Bard and 65% versus DaVinci003

results.claim: Alpaca 65B trained on 52 times more data is less preferred than LIMA.
results.setup: Human preference study, Fig 1: LIMA wins 53% vs Alpaca
results.quote: despite training on 52 times more data, Alpaca 65B

results.claim: GPT-4 prefers LIMA over its own output 19% of the time.
results.quote: even GPT-4 prefers LIMA outputs over its own 19% of the time
results.note: Human study Fig 1 gives 18% LIMA wins vs GPT-4; Section 4.2 text quotes 19% in the GPT-4-annotated context

results.claim: 88% of LIMA responses meet the prompt requirements and 50% are excellent.
results.setup: 50 random test prompts, manual labelling by authors
results.quote: 88% meet the prompt requirements, and 50% are considered excellent.

results.claim: LIMA follows all but 6 of 50 analysed prompts.
results.quote: it is able to follow all but 6 of the 50 analyzed prompts

results.claim: On 20 out-of-distribution prompts LIMA gets 20% fail, 35% pass, 45% excellent.
results.setup: 7 of 50 plus 13 additional prompts with no related training example (43 of 50 had related format)
results.quote: 20% of responses fail, 35% pass, and 45% are excellent

results.claim: LIMA responds safely to 80% of 30 sensitive test prompts, 6 of 10 malicious.
results.setup: 13 safety examples in training; 30 sensitive test prompts
results.quote: LIMA responds safely to 80% of them

results.claim: Filtered, diverse Stack Exchange gives 3.83 versus 3.49 wikiHow and 3.33 unfiltered Stack Exchange.
results.setup: 7B LLaMa, 2,000 examples per source, 5 samples per test prompt, ChatGPT grader
results.table: Figure 5, bars 3.49 (wikiHow), 3.33 (unfiltered Stack Exchange), 3.83 (filtered Stack Exchange)
results.note: Text states a 0.5 point gap for quality filtering; 3.83-3.33=0.50

results.claim: Doubling the training set (up to 16x, 2K to 32K) does not improve response quality.
results.quote: doubling the training set does not improve response quality

results.claim: 30 dialogue chains raise the excellent share of multi-turn responses from 45.2% to 76.1%.
Zero-shot LIMA fails to follow the prompt within 3 interactions in 6 of 10 conversations.
results.setup: LIMA trained on single-turn data only
results.quote: in 6 out of 10 conversations, LIMA fails to follow the prompt within 3 interactions

limits: Authors concede the effort of constructing such examples is significant and hard to scale.
LIMA is not as robust as product-grade models; an unlucky sample or adversarial prompt often gives a weak response.
Safety analysis rests on 30 prompts and 13 training examples; implicit malicious intent often yields unsafe answers.
Diversity ablation compares Stack Exchange to wikiHow, which the authors admit has confounding factors.
Ablations use 7B and a ChatGPT grader; the main result uses 65B and 300 prompts with one sample each.
Groups A and B authors had significant contact, so test prompts share priors with training prompts.
No seeds, hardware or compute are reported; no code or weights link in the text.
Baseline responses were sampled in April 2023; GPT-4, Claude and Bard versions have since changed.

terms.definition: A model's knowledge and capabilities are learnt almost entirely during pretraining, while alignment teaches it which subdistribution of formats should be used when interacting with users.
